pass_meta.suite: Global Search V2 - V1 regression set (section 6769)
pass_meta.how_judged: Every verdict is read from the RENDERED ROWS, using the app's own result-row test ids, with the tab strip's counts, the modal's own result-count line and the /api/search response the page was rendered from all required to agree. Zeros are checked against the seed manifest so a missing record is never reported as a product fault.
pass_meta.po_ruling: The ten open Product Owner questions were answered on 15 September 2026 (Global-Search-questions-ANSWERED-from-V1-2026-09-15.xlsx), every row YES - it should still work, log it as a fault. Eleven cases move from Blocked to Failed as a result.

C55673.observed: Typed a word and pressed Enter without touching the arrow keys. The wrong record opened. Two separate things are wrong. On a long list of results, the row the panel highlights on its own is the eighth, not the first - so Enter opens the eighth record. And once you click a row yourself, that POSITION is remembered: searching again keeps the same row number highlighted, including when you search for a completely different word, where that row holds a record with no connection to what you typed. A short search behaves correctly, which is why this looks fine at first glance - lists of a few results start on the first row. Nothing on screen says which row Enter will open. The QA lead approved raising this on 15 September 2026, after checking the previous version on production himself and confirming that typing a word and pressing Enter there takes you to the first record in the list.
C55673.todo: Pressing Enter should open the top result, and whichever row is going to open should be shown as selected so a person can see where Enter will take them. This needs fixing, and is logged.
C55673.technical: Highlight index with nothing pressed, by list length: 2, 3, 6 and 8 rows -> index 0; 13, 22 and 41 rows -> index 7. After clicking index 4 on 'Truck' (41 rows): same word again -> index 4 highlighted, Enter opened it; different word 'Repair' -> index 4 highlighted, Enter opened /workorders/27eeb282-7196-4b53-a6f1-4f5016022094/lines, unrelated to the click. In an earlier run where the list had shifted, the same index held a different job - so it is the position that persists, not the record. Evidence ENTER-ANNOTATED.json, ENTER-STICKY.json, ENTER-MANY.json; four annotated screenshots in enter-evidence/. CORRECTION: an earlier reading of this case called it a general failure on the strength of two runs of the same query - that was one observation and one replay, since the app remembers the query (L0115).
C55673.ticket: Logged as SV-10061 - "Enter opens the wrong record: the highlight starts on the 8th row of a long list, and once you click a row that position sticks across later searches": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10061

C53605.observed: Typing the year and the make together - '2019 Freightliner', the most natural way anyone would look for a vehicle - returned no vehicles at all. Taken apart, each piece works: the year on its own returns twenty vehicles, the make on its own returns twenty, and the make with the model returns twenty including ours. It is only when the YEAR is combined with another word that everything disappears: '2019 Freightliner', 'Cascadia 2019' and '2019 Cascadia' all return nothing, in either order. The vehicle's record carries the right year, make and model - that was checked and corrected first - and searching its model does find it, so the search is up to date.
C53605.todo: Searching a vehicle by its year together with the make or model needs to work. Both the old product and the written requirements say the year is one of the things a vehicle can be found by, so this is not a decision anyone needs to make - it is simply not working. The useful detail for whoever fixes it: the year on its own is fine, so the year is being recorded; it is combining the year with any second word that empties the results.
C53605.technical: query '2019 Freightliner' -> assets 0; '2019' -> 20; 'Freightliner' -> 20; 'Freightliner Cascadia' -> 20 incl. ZZT-4471 (2019 Freightliner Cascadia). '2019 Cascadia' and 'Cascadia 2019' also 0. Asset year/make/model verified on the record before the run. Spec v1.5 section 4 indexes asset year.
C53605.ticket: Logged as SV-10055 - "a vehicle cannot be found by its year together with its make or model": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10055

C53587.observed: A new job was created and then searched for by its number, over and over, without reloading or signing out. It did not come back until about 85 seconds had passed. The requirement allows 30. The method is not in doubt, and two separate controls prove it: a new CUSTOMER, created and timed exactly the same way in the same session, came back after 17 seconds; and a new PART SALE for 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', created and timed the same way, came back after 9 seconds. So the clock and the search can both see a brand new record well inside the allowed window - jobs are the one kind that cannot.
C53587.todo: A newly created job needs to be findable within 30 seconds, as the requirement says and as a new part sale and a new customer both already manage. Useful detail for whoever looks: part sales and customers appear within seconds and jobs do not, so jobs are not being refreshed the same way as the rest. The receive-a-part flow still needs running once.
C53587.technical: new work order: findable at ~85s, first hit poll 85s, requirement 30s (spec v1.5 section 9). Controls in the same session: new customer 17s, new part sale P9160-254 9s. No reload, no re-auth between polls.
C53587.ticket: Logged as SV-10056 - "a newly created job is not findable for about 85 seconds": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10056
C53587.not_observed: One of the three flows in this case was not run: receiving a part through Receive Order was not exercised. The new-job flow and the new-part-sale flow were both timed.

C45148.observed: Across roughly seventy searches in this pass the results only ever contained the nine kinds of record the panel is built to show - jobs, customers, vehicles, parts, suppliers, part sales, purchase orders, supplier invoices - and nothing else ever appeared. The stronger evidence is what a limited person sees: a technician, who has no access to parts or suppliers, got no parts and no suppliers at all and no headings for them, while a foreman searching the same word got both. What a person is not permitted is not shown.
C45148.not_observed: A genuinely new or unknown kind of record cannot be introduced from outside the product, so the case cannot be pushed further than this from the screen.

C45142.observed: No job on this branch withholds jobs while allowing anything else - every one of the eleven allows jobs. The closest available person sees nothing at all, which does not answer this case: it cannot tell you whether jobs specifically are withheld.
